learning_outcomes.text: You apply the basic principles of project-based work through a multidisciplinary project on a concrete socially relevant Tech&IT issue.
You draw up a structured project plan that takes into account phasing, roles, time, risks, and quality control.
You critically reflect on your own role within the team and on the collaboration with students from other disciplines, using, among other things, the Johari window and core competencies.
You have insight into techniques to present a project proposal in a clear, structured, and impactful way, adapted to the audience and context.

syllabus_topics: Roles and responsibilities within a project (stakeholders)
Project phasing and importance of a good Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
Content and importance of project plan: time management, project control (incl. risk management), budget control, resource planning, quality assurance and delivery.
Multidisciplinary project proposal with a societal focus (mobility, care technology, industry…): drafting of a project plan according to the basic principles of Project Management
Formulating and presenting a project proposal to a specific target audience
Reflection on the collaboration (task and role distribution) and communication
assessment_rules: The total assessment is on a 1-20 scale. There will be two peer assessments; the first is for practice and learning, and the second is used to calculate a peer factor for each individual student, which informs the lecturer's individual grade. The resit opportunity involves the same modalities as the first examination opportunity. There are no partial transfers for this course.
